lesson.text: Remember? A fact text has headings and a main idea. Today you write two kinds of text: an opinion and a fact text.
A fact can be checked and proved true: "A spider has eight legs." An opinion is what someone thinks or feels: "Spiders are the most amazing animals."
Opinion writing: say your opinion, give reasons with because, since and for example, and end with a sentence that sums it up. "Dogs make great pets because they are loyal and fun."
Linking words join your reasons: because, since, for example, also, another reason is, so.
A fact text: start with the topic, group the facts under headings, explain new words, and end with a sentence that sums it up.
Use facts, not feelings, in a fact text: "Owls hunt at night", not "Owls are the best". Check your facts in a book you trust.

Try it in the world: write a sign for your favourite place in your world. Give one fact ("This lake is 20 blocks wide") and one opinion ("It is the best place to fish"). Next, in grade 4: writing an opinion.

exercises.prompt: Which one is a fact?
exercises.hint: Can you check it and prove it?
exercises.explain: You can count the legs: that is a fact.

exercises.prompt: Which one is an opinion?
exercises.hint: Which one is what someone thinks?
choices: Pizza is baked in an oven.
exercises.explain: "Tastiest" is what someone thinks.

exercises.prompt: An opinion needs reasons to make it strong.
exercises.hint: Why should the reader agree?
exercises.explain: True: reasons help the reader understand your opinion.

exercises.prompt: Which word gives a reason?
exercises.hint: Which word answers why?
exercises.explain: Because gives a reason.

exercises.prompt: Which is the best reason for "Dogs make great pets"?
exercises.hint: The reason must support the opinion.
exercises.explain: Loyal and friendly explains why dogs are great pets.

exercises.prompt: Put the opinion paragraph in order.
exercises.hint: Start with the opinion; end by summing up.
items: Another reason is that we make friends.
It helps us move our bodies.
I think playtime should be longer.
exercises.explain: Opinion, reason, another reason, then the ending.

exercises.prompt: Which heading fits these facts? "Owls eat mice. They also eat insects."
exercises.hint: What are the facts about?
exercises.explain: Both facts are about food.

exercises.prompt: "Owls are the best birds" belongs in a fact text.
exercises.hint: Is it a fact or an opinion?
exercises.explain: False: it is an opinion. A fact text uses facts.

exercises.prompt: Which linking word adds another reason?
exercises.hint: You want to say one more thing.
exercises.explain: Also adds another reason.

exercises.prompt: Which is the best ending for a text about owls?
exercises.hint: An ending sums up the main idea.
choices: Owls are clever hunters of the night.
exercises.explain: It sums up what the text taught.

exercises.prompt: Fix the mistake in this fact text: "Frogs lay eggs. Frogs are the cutest. Frogs can jump far."
exercises.hint: Which sentence is an opinion?
exercises.explain: "The cutest" is an opinion, so it does not belong in a fact text.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence gives an example?
exercises.hint: Look for the linking words for example.
choices: For example, a dog can learn to fetch.
exercises.explain: For example shows an example that supports the reason.

exercises.prompt: Where should the fact "Owls nest in old barns" go?
exercises.hint: Group facts under the right heading.
choices: under the heading Where Owls Live
under the heading What Owls Eat
exercises.explain: Nests are about where owls live.

exercises.prompt: A fact text should end with a sentence that sums it up.
exercises.hint: Think of how the owl text ends.
exercises.explain: True: a closing sentence sums up the topic.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence joins an opinion and a reason?
exercises.hint: Look for an opinion word and because.
choices: I love snow because I can build snowmen.
exercises.explain: "I love snow" is the opinion and "because I can build snowmen" is the reason.

exercises.prompt: Sort them: fact or opinion?
exercises.hint: Can it be checked and proved?
exercises.explain: Facts: eight legs, frozen water. Opinions: scary, the best.

exercises.prompt: Match each linking word to its job.
matches: shows what happens as a result
exercises.hint: Try each one in a sentence about dogs, and hear what it does.
exercises.explain: Because gives a reason, for example shows one case, and so shows a result.

exercises.prompt: Which belongs in a fact text, and which in opinion writing?
exercises.hint: A fact text teaches; opinion writing persuades.
exercises.explain: Headings and explained words belong in a fact text; reasons with because and what you think belong in opinion writing.

exercises.prompt: Sort the linking words by their job.
exercises.hint: Does it say why, show one case, or add another point?
exercises.explain: Reasons: because, since. An example: for example. Adding more: also, another reason is.

exercises.prompt: Order a short fact text about owls.
items: To sum up: owls are night hunters.
Owls are birds that hunt at night.
Their big eyes see in the dark.
exercises.hint: Start with the topic, then a fact, then the sentence that sums it up.
exercises.explain: Start with the topic (owls hunt at night), give a fact that explains it (their big eyes see in the dark), then sum it up at the end.
